theme: whole-text structural profile and language-family typology
question: Does a structural profile of Indus texts separate candidate language families when compared with readable seal and record corpora?
outcome: Indus initial-sign entropy exceeds final-sign entropy: asymmetry +0.260 against a shuffle range of -0.017 to 0.018, and +0.149 without the 35.2% of texts ending in 740. In comparison corpora the statistic changes sign with unit and genre: Ur III seal legends score -0.204 by sign and +0.079 by word. It is therefore descriptive, and every candidate language remains tied under the frozen rule.
challenge: Segment statistics became unreliable after the rehearsal. The numeral-order calibration failed on Ur III because of the value definition, and the typology table is unverified.
remedy: A pre-computation amendment substituted whole-text statistics. The calibration cause is reported, and the typology status is stated.
retry_when: At least two head-initial and two head-final seal-legend corpora are measured at sign and word level with the same code.
